[EFFECT] Weather conditions affect bike demand in a step-like fashion across the four categories. Clear skies (category 1) give the model a small positive boost to predicted demand, while mist or cloudy conditions (category 2) produce a slight drag near zero. Light rain or snow (category 3) causes a large, consistent drop in predicted demand — contributions fall to around –0.2 to –0.6 in log space, translating to a meaningful reduction in expected rentals. The handful of heavy rain hours (category 4) also show negative contributions, though the rare occurrence limits how confidently the model can characterise that category.

[IMPORTANCE] Weathersit ranks 7th out of 9 features, with an importance score of 0.051 — far below the top drivers such as hour of day (0.83), year (0.20), and temperature (0.20). It exerts a real but relatively modest influence on predicted demand, sitting just above wind speed and holiday in terms of overall impact.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because light rain and snow consistently suppress demand, operations teams can use weather forecasts to proactively reduce bike availability or delay morning/evening rebalancing runs on days where precipitation is expected, helping to avoid under-utilised bikes sitting at stations during low-demand periods.
